rules.name: node_modules
rules.what: Every package this project depends on, installed from its package.json and lockfile.
rules.comeback: Run your package manager's install command (npm install, yarn, pnpm install or bun install) and it is rebuilt exactly from the lockfile.

rules.name: .next
rules.what: Next.js build output and its development cache.
rules.comeback: Created again the next time you run next dev or next build.

rules.name: .nuxt and .output
rules.what: Files Nuxt generates while developing and building your app.
rules.comeback: Generated again by nuxt dev or nuxt build.

rules.name: .svelte-kit
rules.what: Generated types and build files for a SvelteKit project.
rules.comeback: SvelteKit generates it again whenever you run dev or build.

rules.name: .turbo
rules.what: Turborepo's local task cache, so unchanged tasks can be skipped.
rules.comeback: Filled again as tasks run. The first run afterwards is just slower.

rules.name: .parcel-cache
rules.comeback: Parcel rebuilds it on the next build.

rules.name: npm cache
rules.what: A copy of every package npm has ever downloaded, kept to speed up installs.
rules.comeback: npm downloads packages again the next time an install needs them.

rules.name: Yarn cache
rules.what: Packages Yarn has downloaded, shared across projects.
rules.comeback: Yarn fetches packages again on the next install.

rules.name: pnpm store
rules.what: pnpm's shared package store. Your projects' node_modules folders are hard links into it, so moving it frees almost nothing until those projects are cleaned too.
rules.comeback: pnpm's own prune command removes only packages no project uses, which is the safe way to shrink it.

rules.name: Bun install cache
rules.what: Packages Bun has downloaded, shared across projects.
rules.comeback: Bun downloads packages again on the next install.

rules.name: Deno cache
rules.what: Remote modules and compiled code Deno has cached.
rules.comeback: Deno downloads and compiles modules again when a script needs them.

rules.name: node-gyp headers
rules.what: Node.js headers downloaded to compile native add-ons.
rules.comeback: node-gyp downloads the headers again the next time a native package builds.
